I farm the way I know best: steady, not risky, and matched to my age, land, and water. I have only 9 mu, but I have grown wheat and maize for many years on the same wheat-maize rotation, so I will keep the full 9 mu in winter wheat and then plant summer maize on the same 9 mu after wheat harvest. Because I am 72 and my household labor is limited, I will not do anything too complicated. I will use reliable seed, keep fertilizer at a moderate level, irrigate when the crop really needs it because I have well water, and avoid too many pesticide sprays unless pressure becomes obvious. For wheat, I will focus on stable tillering, enough water at key stages, and a solid but not excessive fertilizer program. For maize, I will move quickly after wheat harvest, use hybrid seed for stable production, reduce tillage to save labor and time, and keep water and fertilizer sufficient for grain filling. What I want most is a dependable harvest with manageable cost and labor, not chasing the absolute highest yield.
